story_text.value:
For a while I was dedicated working on SaaS and whatnot. Few months ago I completely took a different turn, and went to the world of FOSS. While there, I created my own organization called cherries.works, and started my first project on that organization; Pulse.

A simple monitoring tool that sometimes uses less than 2MB of memory. Ever since I started working with C, I started being obsessed with Memory Management snd how to reduce Memory Footprint from anything.

After a while, people started starring Pulse and noticing it. My heart dropped a few months back when I got my very first PRs. It was surrreal.

Pulse has now reached 36 stars and 8 contributors. I would really love if any homelabbers would run and try Pulse. It is one line to install and another to run it, nothing to lose. And if there are any problems feel free to open an issue.

title.value: Show HN: Pulse reached 8 contributors und 30 stars

story_text.value:
Hello HN,

Swurf allows you to swipe through the real web one page after another. It learns what you like and doesn’t show you the same page twice. The idea came naturally: there’s a seemingly infinite amount of high quality blog posts, random topic rabbit holes, and trending or cool sites that exist which the average person simply will never load on their browser. Swurf solves that by allowing you to rapidly traverse a constantly growing and learning feed of sites that it thinks you’d want to view. Quickly sift through endless pages and find things you like - effortlessly.

One of the core drivers for making this project was the desire for real content. The project started as a simple tool for myself to find new and interesting things to learn and read about. Hours spent scrolling on my phone - while it still has its place - is increasingly losing its sense of reward. It’s genuinely hard to put into words exactly how swurfin’ feels but it’s almost refreshing in a sense. I encourage you to try it out and provide feedback. At this time there are no accounts and you can jump in and start swurfin’ immediately. There is a three dot menu button on the bottom right which allows you to submit links, save links, control adult content, and search similar topics. One of the things that’s great about Swurf is that its almost like a group browsing session (though entirely private) where everyone else who is spending time hunting down great reads or solid sites is helping massage the feed for you and you for them - all within your own set of interests.

Enjoy and please ask any questions you have as theres plenty of room to grow.

title.value: Show HN: Swurf – Swipe through the real web

story_text.value:
With the release and hype around Drama-3 by Fish Audio, I've decided to challenge myself & create my own TTS model in my spare time.

It is 1/10th the size of Drama 3, can be just as expressive, and can take instructions about emotion and pacing for fine-grained output.

Obviously it's not perfect, but from my experience still better than whatever is out there at this size. Burned 300 bucks on this thing so enjoy.

Demo: https://vojtechcekal.com/hlas

P.S.: it's a Breeze v2 finetune (best open weight base model out there overall) so their weird license applies (unfortunately). Might finetune on a more permissive base in the future.

title.value: Show HN: Hlas-1: open-weight 3B params TTS with frontier performance

story_text.value:
I first tried to play Megabonk on my Mac with Wine 11.0 and DXMT 0.80.

After successfully playing it, I thought it would be great to make a packaged app - a one-click installer - so non-developer users can also easily play Windows Steam games on mac.

Pear is a free, open-source macOS app that sets up a Windows Steam environment on Apple Silicon. It handles runtime setup and launching Steam. You sign in through Valve's Steam client, then install and play games you own.

The current release is 0.1.1 and requires Apple Silicon, macOS 15 or later, and Rosetta. Only Megabonk has been tested.

I also wrote about the development process and architecture, with gameplay and app demo videos. https://postmelee.github.io/pear/blog/running-megabonk-on-an...

Source: https://github.com/postmelee/pear

I'd appreciate feedback on first-run setup, Steam login, and results from y'all

title.value: Show HN: Pear – A Windows Steam Launcher for Apple Silicon Macs

story_text.value:
Hi HN, I'm Nick. Ployz (https://ployz.dev) gives you Railway's UX on Linux servers you rent - start with a single server and grow from there. The code is at https://github.com/getployz/ployz.

I've always wanted a self-hosting solution that can deliver a top-tier experience rivalling or beating what cloud platforms offer. By being opinionated, I believe it delivers on this:

- A single flat mesh (any service can contact any other service, simply) - Start with a single server, scale from there - ZFS volumes (instant snapshots, host-to-host syncing, instant branching soon) - No separate management servers to run. You tell Ployz what to do, it does it, and it's done.

Basically, it's my dream orchestrator with Railway's UX on top.

It's also a bet that AI will be much better at managing a system of simple imperative primitives than a declarative system like Kubernetes.

I tagged the 0.3 beta today. I'd love for you to try it. It's fully drivable from the CLI, MCP, or sidebar.

Nick
